newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bkk Bank of Commerce approves IFCT takeover.
newsitem.headline: Bkk Bank of Commerce approves IFCT takeover.

text.p: Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc shareholders on Wednesday approved plans for the Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand to takeover the running of the ailing bank on May 2, its officials said.

The signing of a contract allowing semi-government industrial lender IFCT to take over an 18.5 percent stake in the bank and manage it would preface the dissolution of the bank's state-appointed management committee and the first meeting of a new BBC main board, the officials said.
Four members of the current IFCT executive will be on the new 11-man bank main board, a bank spokesman told Reuters.
The central bank and the Thai Finance Ministry took over the running of the bank in May last year following revelations that the it was saddled with a massive non-performing loan problem.
The bank has estimated that after collateral reduction it had net non-performing loans of 53.78 billion baht at end-1996.

"After the contract is signed on Friday, we can expect the Finance Minister to dissolve the control committee. Then we should see a meeting of the bank's new board. That would be the chronological sequence," said a vice-president of the bank, Viravudhi Vajrabhaya.
The contract, giving IFCT an option to increase its stake in the bank over a seven year period to 51 percent at pre-determined prices, is a largely risk-free opportunity, analysts said.

"We see benefits for IFCT in its role as manager and as a potential equity participant in the bank," said Vickers Ballas bank analyst Andrew Maule. "IFCT will receive benefits in the form of a management fee and profit sharing without having any exposure to or legal responsibility for the bank's poor loan portfolio."
IFCT is to receive 36 million baht per year for managing the bank, while the central bank takes over responsibility for the bank's problem loans burden.

"IFCT has ... a put option allowing it to redeem its shares to the FIDF (central bank fund) at a predetermined price ... the downside risk of IFCT's role in the rehabilitation appears very limited," he said.
Although the future of the bank now appears more secure the bank's ability to return to profit as quickly as the new management would like it to is less certain, analysts said.
The bank reported a loss of 24.85 billion baht in 1996, a sum greater than any Thai commercial bank has either made or lost in a single year, and will have to further raise provisioning.

With capital increases likely to be required over the next two years, analysts said investors should exercise caution before buying the bank's stock despite substantial recent gains in its pared price.

The shares, which resumed trading on April 17 after an 11 month suspension, continued a recent strong rally on Wednesday ending up 0.70 baht to 8.10 baht after falling nearly 75 percent of their value on resumption of trading.
Brokers said existing shareholders may be buying to bring down the average costs of existing holdings.
"The bank is worth only 3.40 baht per share on a straight book value basis without taking into account any additional NPLs (non-performing loans) that may eventually emerge," said Maule.

"As a result of the restructuring and management support from IFCT, it will survive. However it still faces severe challenges to improve its asset quality and return to profitability ... at a time when core profitability and asset quality of Thai banks are deteriorating," he said.
